q1.why: 1 places the epicenter on the surface directly above where the quake originates; the farm and depth are setting.

q2.why: 13 says one seismograph gives a distance that plots as a circle of infinite possibilities; 14 and 15 cover two and three stations.

q3.why: 15 says only a third seismograph gives a precise location, and 16 and 34 state the minimum of three.

q4.why: 23 and 24 say damage spreads along the rupture and directivity moves the strongest shaking away from the epicenter; 25 is the Denali example.

q5.why: 11 has P arriving before S, 12 derives distance from known velocities, 31 uses the time difference to get distance to the epicenter.

q6.why: 45 allows only a macroseismic epicenter for unrecorded quakes, and 43-44 say it is estimated from intensity data and knowledge of local faults.
